title: Difficult airway: oxygenate first, follow the plan
subject: anaesthesia
summary: Call for help early, preoxygenate and position well, limit laryngoscopy attempts, oxygenate with supraglottic airway or mask, wake the patient if safe, and proceed without delay to emergency front of neck access when intubation and oxygenation both fail. Confirm every tube with waveform capnography. No drug doses are stated; drug charts and local DAS charts govern them.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Predict difficulty from history, mouth opening, neck movement, dentition and previous records, and still expect the unanticipated difficult airway.
The priority at every step is oxygenation, not intubation at any cost.

sections.title: First actions
items: Call for help early, optimise position, preoxygenate well, and have suction, adjuncts and a supraglottic airway ready before induction.
Declare the plan aloud so the team shares the sequence and fixation error is challenged.

sections.title: Plan sequence
items: Plan A is optimised laryngoscopy with limited attempts. Repeated trauma closes the airway.
Plan B is a supraglottic airway to oxygenate. Plan C is face mask ventilation and waking the patient if safe.
Cannot intubate and cannot oxygenate means emergency front of neck access without delay, while oxygenation attempts continue.

sections.title: Confirmation and aftercare
items: Confirm every tracheal tube with waveform capnography. No trace means assume oesophageal placement until proved otherwise.
Document what worked, inform the patient, and arrange follow up and an airway alert for future care.

sources.org: Difficult Airway Society and Association of Anaesthetists
